title: Constructive Root Bounds from Descartes Rule of Signs

problemStatement.formal: For p ∈ ℝ[X] nonzero: (1) positive real roots are bounded by sign variations, (2) all roots lie in [-cauchyBound, cauchyBound], (3) zero sign variations certifies no positive roots.
problemStatement.plain: Constructive root bounds from Descartes' rule of signs: sign variation counts bound positive root counts, Cauchy bounds localize all roots, and zero sign variations certify root-free intervals.
whyMatters: Foundational tool in computational algebra for root isolation
Connects sign variation combinatorics to analytic root counting

proven: root_free_certificate_positive: nonneg coefficients → no positive roots
linear examples, IVT-based root existence, Cauchy bound computations
